title: Taro Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Taro Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Taro nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus in gabi, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Taro nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your gabi (taro) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, calcium, magnesium, sulfur, iron and zinc. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Taro leaf scorched brown along the edges and between the veins from potassium shortage
heroImage.credit: Scot Nelson (photo by Douglas Hunefeld Photograph), CC0 1.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But calcium, sulfur, iron and zinc stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which taro nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a taro nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest taro nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in taro

Roots, main shoot and suckers stay stunted. Yellowing starts on the oldest leaf blades and, as it gets worse, all the blades turn yellow. Old leaves die early, so fewer leaves are working and the corm yield drops. You see it most at this stage: from 2 months after planting through corm bulking.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in gabi
Flooded (wetland) taro loses nitrogen to the air when the soil has no oxygen. Taro does best when most of the nitrogen in the soil is nitrate.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur deficiency yellows the young leaves evenly. Magnesium deficiency yellows between the veins of old leaves. To be sure, test leaf number 2, the second fully open leaf below the newest. Below 4.0 percent nitrogen means it is short. A leaf test confirms it.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Apply nitrogen following the soil test, for example Urea 46 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14 in split doses. You can also give a urea spray of 10 g per liter (160 g in a 16 liter sprayer) every 15 days. Do not overdo it, since too much nitrogen invites taro leaf blight. A usual side dress is 1 to 2 bags of Urea 46 0 0 or 2 to 4 bags of Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 per hectare, 30 to 45 days after planting.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea (46 0 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Ammonium Chloride** by La Filipina (25 0 0), **Agripower 46 0 0 (Locally Blended) Coated** by Green Acres Agri Tech and **Calcipro** by Ramgo (15.5 0 0 with 18.8 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, split nitrogen through the season and add compost or manure.
Potassium deficiency in taro

blocks.alt: Taro leaf scorched brown along the edges and between the veins from potassium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Scot Nelson (photo by Douglas Hunefeld Photograph), CC0 1.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Growth slows, plants wilt easily and leaf blades are smaller. Older leaves get a burnt look between the veins or along the edges. In some varieties irregular brown spots form in the center of older blades and join until the whole leaf yellows or browns. Corms stay small. You see it most at this stage: corm bulking.
Why potassium deficiency happens in gabi
Sandy and leached soils, and fields where taro and other root crops have been grown for years.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency yellows between veins first, then browns the margins. Taro leaf blight gives water soaked spots that ooze, mainly in wet weather. To be sure, leaf test of leaf number 2. Soil test for potassium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 following the soil test, split in parts. Give a potassium sulfate spray of 10 g per liter (160 g in a 16 liter sprayer) as a quick fix. A usual dose is 2 to 3 bags of Muriate of potash 0 0 60 per hectare, half at planting and half when the roots or tubers start to swell.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash (MOP)** by Atlas Fertilizer (0 0 60), **Simplot Sulfate 0 0 50** by Nutranta, **Potassium Nitrate** by Parafield (13 0 46) and **Qrop Mix Production 14 0 23 plus 13 Cao** by Farmtech Agriland (14 0 23 with 9.3 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, return crop waste and add wood ash or compost.
Phosphorus deficiency in taro

Root and shoot growth are stunted. Older leaf blades can look darker green, and in some varieties many light colored dots form between the veins. Later the leaf edges yellow and turn brown. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in gabi
Acid upland soils and volcanic soils that hold phosphorus. In flooded fields phosphorus becomes more available.
How to tell it apart
Potassium deficiency gives brown spots and scorched edges, not light dots on dark leaves. To be sure, do a soil test and a leaf test. A leaf holding 0.3 to 0.5 percent phosphorus has enough.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency
Use single superphosphate for a quick fix and rock phosphate for the long term, following the soil test. A usual basal dose is 4 to 6 bags of Complete 14 14 14 per hectare in the furrow at planting.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Philphos 18 46 0 (Di Ammonium Phosphate)**, **Atlas Super Gro (16 20 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Granular Single Super Phosphate** by La Filipina (0 18 0 with 11 percent sulfur) and **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals (0 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, apply phosphorus at planting and add organic manure.
Calcium deficiency in taro

Root and shoot growth drop and roots look stunted. The newest blade yellows between the veins first. When it is bad, blades cup and brown at the margins, never open fully, and the shoot dies. Dying roots let soil diseases in. You see it most at this stage: early growth, on acid upland soils.
Why calcium deficiency happens in gabi
Very acid soils. At pH 4, aluminum also poisons the roots. Heavy potash or ammonium fertilizer, salty soil and dry spells keep calcium from reaching fruit and young leaves.
How to tell it apart

Manganese toxicity in older leaves can look like calcium deficiency with cupped blades. Calcium deficiency starts on the youngest leaf. To be sure, test the soil pH and a leaf. Below 0.7 percent calcium in the leaf means it is short. A soil test for calcium and pH, and a leaf test, confirm it.
What to apply for calcium deficiency
On acid soils, lime about 250 kg per hectare where the pH is 5.5 to 6. About 840 kg per hectare in two splits where it is 3.5 to 4.5. Dolomite protects taro roots on soils with toxic aluminum.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** (36.2 percent calcium), **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Calcipro** by Ramgo (15.5 0 0 with 18.8 percent calcium) and **Philphos Gypsum** (22.2 percent calcium and 17.4 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils ahead of planting. Test the soil every two or three years. Keep potash in balance with magnesium and calcium.
Magnesium deficiency in taro

Older leaf blades yellow between the veins while the veins stay dark green. As it gets worse the margins and the spaces between veins turn brown and die, leaves may curl and drop early. You see it most at this stage: mid season.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in gabi
Sandy soils, acid soils and heavy potash.
How to tell it apart
Potassium deficiency scorches margins without the clear green vein pattern. To be sure, A leaf test below 0.2 percent magnesium means it is short.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

Give about 80 kg magnesium sulfate per hectare in bands near the plants. Do not apply it together with potash. Use Dolomite on acid soils. Put the soil dose in before planting or when the rains begin. Sprays show results in 10 to 14 days.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Agsmart Kieserite Granule** (20 percent sulfur and 16.3 percent magnesium), **DDDD Planter's Choice Magnesium Sulphate Monohydrate** by Modern Time (15.1 percent magnesium) and **Zetryl MAG 9** by Zetryl Chem (9 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils with dolomite. Test the soil every two or three years.
Sulfur deficiency in taro

Roots and shoots grow less, leaf blades are smaller, and the younger leaves turn evenly yellow. The yellow is uniform across the blade, without a pattern of green veins. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why sulfur deficiency happens in gabi
Soils low in organic matter and burning crop waste.
How to tell it apart

Nitrogen deficiency yellows the old leaves first. To be sure, A leaf holding under 0.2 percent sulfur is short. A soil test for sulfur and a leaf test confirm it. In a soil test, less than 10 ppm of sulfate sulfur is low.
What to apply for sulfur deficiency
Use Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 or single superphosphate. Give about 25 kg sulfur dust per hectare on sulfur poor soils, or Gypsum on alkaline soils. Give it at planting or with the first side dress.

Sold here with sulfur: **Atlas Ammosul 21 0 0** by Atlas Fertilizer (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur), **Philphos Gypsum** (22.2 percent calcium and 17.4 percent sulfur), **Harvester Sulphate of Potash** by Universal Harvester (0 0 50 with 17.5 percent sulfur) and **Agsmart Kieserite Granule** (20 percent sulfur and 16.3 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [ammonium sulfate fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), and the page on [sulfur deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/sulfur-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add organic matter. Test the soil every two or three years.
Iron deficiency in taro
Younger leaf blades first yellow between the veins, then turn evenly bleached. Fewer side roots form. You see it most at this stage: early growth, in upland taro.
Why iron deficiency happens in gabi
Upland (not flooded) soils with high pH. Flooding makes iron more available. Too much manganese can also block iron.
How to tell it apart

Manganese toxicity on older leaves looks like iron deficiency but starts on the old blades. Manganese deficiency also starts on young leaves. To be sure, test leaf number 2. Below 100 ppm iron means it is short. A soil pH test and a leaf test of the young leaves confirm it.
What to apply for iron deficiency
Give about 15 kg ferrous sulfate per hectare to the soil, following a soil test. Spray the young leaves in the cool of the day, soon after sunrise or near sunset.

Sold here with iron: **DDDD Planter's Choice Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Modern Time (19 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl Chem (30 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulphate Monohydrate** by Newman Chemicals (30 percent iron) and **Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep organic matter high in upland taro fields.
Zinc deficiency in taro
Taro low in zinc is stunted above and below ground, and other signs can be faint. Smaller, distorted young leaves in a rosette and slow leaf growth. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why zinc deficiency happens in gabi
Soils outside pH 5 to 7.5 and heavy phosphorus.
How to tell it apart
Many problems stunt taro. Only a leaf test confirms zinc. To be sure, A leaf test of 20 to 40 ppm zinc means the plant has enough.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Give about 20 kg Zinc sulfate per hectare to the soil, or a spray of 2 g zinc sulfate with 2.5 g lime per liter in severe cases. Keep zinc and phosphate applications apart. Give the soil dose at planting or when the rains begin, and sprays on young growth.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester (22 percent zinc), **Petbowe Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** (33 percent zinc), **Tierramino ZN** by Unilox Far East Resources (7 0 0 with 10 percent zinc) and **Liquid Chelate Zinc with Sulfur** by Sagrex (10 percent zinc and 5 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, test before adding zinc. Too much is toxic to taro. Test the soil every two or three years.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any taro nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your gabi needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Taro nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my gabi leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: older leaf blades yellow first, then all of them, with stunted plants and few suckers. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at calcium deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in taro?
items.a: Apply nitrogen following the soil test, for example Urea 46 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14 in split doses. You can also give a urea spray of 10 g per liter (160 g in a 16 liter sprayer) every 15 days.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in taro?
items.a: Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 following the soil test, split in parts. Give a potassium sulfate spray of 10 g per liter (160 g in a 16 liter sprayer) as a quick fix.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in taro?
items.a: Use single superphosphate for a quick fix and rock phosphate for the long term, following the soil test. A usual basal dose is 4 to 6 bags of Complete 14 14 14 per hectare in the furrow at planting.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my gabi lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the taro nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
